dedupe_keys.name: brick schema ontology for building metadata

description: Brick is an open-source ontology that standardises semantic descriptions of the physical, logical and virtual assets in buildings and the relationships between them, maintained by the Brick Consortium. It has three parts: an RDF class hierarchy of building subsystems, equipment and points; a small set of relationships that link entities into a directed graph of a building; and a way to compose complex components from simpler ones. It covers HVAC, lighting, fire, security and other subsystems in one cross-vendor representation, and the repository includes examples such as a small apartment and ASHRAE Guideline 36 figures. Coverage: any building; the ontology is not tied to a place. Access: releases and documentation from the website and repository, with minor releases targeted about every six months. Licence: BSD 3-Clause; free. Caveats: a model of a real building still has to be written for each site, and mappings from building management system labels are manual or tool-assisted. Simulation uses are a common metadata layer linking sensor data, control points and equipment to building energy and fault models and to digital twins. Related records: Project Haystack, RealEstateCore, ASHRAE Standard 223P and the Google Digital Buildings ontology.
